title: Contraction in Global Grain Exports Still Expected
section_path: Contraction in Global Grain Exports Still Expected
section_path_text: Contraction in Global Grain Exports Still Expected
summary:
Main
By Jeffrey Landsberg
As we discussed in Commodore Research's most recent Weekly Executive Report, the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) has released its latest forecast for the 2026/27 season and is now predicting that global coarse grain, wheat, soybean, and soymeal exports will total 745 million tons. This is 1.3 million tons less than the USDA predicted a month ago - and it is 21.3 million tons (-3%) less than is expected for the 2025/26 season. The forecast is still preliminary, but a year-on-year decline in exports would be a headwind for our market.
